# Configure the MCP Sidecar

This page describes how to configure the [MCP Sidecar](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/tool-access) on Kubernetes. You register AI agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers so that agent tool calls travel through the sidecar.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Requirements

- Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric installed with the [`ai.agent.image`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-ai-agent-image) Helm value set. Refer to [Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install).

## Register AI agents

Annotate the pod template of each AI agent with the `ai-agent` role. Consul injects the MCP Sidecar into the pod. The sidecar also runs the on-behalf-of identity processor and the human approval server.

<CodeBlockConfig highlight="5">

```yaml
template:
  metadata:
    annotations:
      consul.hashicorp.com/connect-inject: "true"
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role: ai-agent
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

The sidecar uses the defaults in the [`AgentConfig`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/agentconfig) resource. The following table lists the defaults and the annotations that override them for one pod.

| Setting | Default | Annotation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent interceptor port | `21101` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-interceptor-port` |
| MCP connectivity port | `15101` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-mcp-port` |
| Human approval server port | `16101` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-hitl-port` |
| Human approval timeout | `60s` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-hitl-approval-timeout` |

The sidecar listens on a Unix domain socket by default. In local development, or where a shared socket volume is unavailable, set `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-addr` to switch the listener to TCP. Refer to [Kubernetes annotations and labels](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/annotation-label) for details.

## Register MCP servers

Annotate the pod template of each in-mesh MCP server with the `mcp-server` role. Consul registers the service with the `mcp-server` role and adds an MCP router filter to the pod's inbound Envoy listener.

<CodeBlockConfig highlight="5">

```yaml
template:
  metadata:
    annotations:
      consul.hashicorp.com/connect-inject: "true"
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role: mcp-server
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

The registration uses the defaults in the [`McpServerConfig`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/mcpserverconfig) resource. The following table lists the defaults and the annotations that override them for one pod.

| Setting | Default | Annotation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP transport | `streamable-http` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-mcp-server-transport` |
| MCP path | `/mcp` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-mcp-server-path` |
| MCP protocol version | `2025-03-26` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-mcp-server-protocol-version` |

## Connect agents to MCP servers

Add each MCP server as an explicit upstream of the agent, and create a service intention that allows the agent to call the server. Consul also uses the agent's explicit upstreams to decide the audiences for on-behalf-of token exchange. Refer to [Configure OAuth clients for AI agents and MCP servers](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/identity/configure-oauth-clients).

To reach an MCP server outside the mesh, route the call through a terminating gateway. Refer to [Configure external credential injection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection/configure).

## Configure tool access and human approval

<!-- TODO: Document how operators define per-tool access policy and which tool calls require human approval. The MCP Sidecar processor source is not in consul-enterprise v2.1.0+ent or consul-k8s v2.1.0. -->

The MCP Sidecar applies per-tool policy and holds protected tool calls for human approval. For how the sidecar evaluates tool calls and approvals, refer to [MCP Sidecar](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/tool-access#discovery-and-invocation).
